newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse sees warrants starting trade end Q3.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse sees warrants starting trade end Q3.

text.p: Warrants should start trade on the Warsaw bourse at the end of 1997's third quarter, a bourse deputy president told daily Parkiet in its Thursday edition.

"At third quarter's end we plan to add warrants to Warsaw bourse trade," Wlodzimierz Magiera was quoted as saying, adding that futures trade on the large-cap WIG 20 index should start in the fourth quarter.
In May the bourse approved rules paving the way for trade in warrants on shares, bonds, stock indices and exchange and interest rates.
The bourse said the minimum size of the warrant issue would be 10,000 and their expiry period should not be shorter than three months.
The minium value of the underlying bonds or shares was set at three million zlotys.
